A Michelin-Starred Journey Through Modern Vietnam
Sep 2026 • Couples
Coco Dining is the kind of restaurant that rewards curiosity. From the outside, it is wonderfully understated — a discreet, modern entrance in dark tones, clean lines and subtle lighting. Nothing shouts for attention. Instead, there is a quiet elegance that draws you in and prepares you for something special.

And special it certainly was.

Coco Dining presents a tasting menu structured around five beautiful chapters: Cultivation, Preservation, Synthesis, Heirloom and Sweet Memory. Coco Dining is not merely about eating an exceptional meal. It is about experiencing a story — and perhaps creating a few memories of your own along the way.

Cultivation takes us back to origins and rice fields.
Preservation explores fermentation, pickling and curing.
Synthesis shows how each encounter adds another layer to identity.
Heirloom reflects the everyday rituals of growing, cooking and sharing.
And finally, Sweet Memory considers what remains — those traces of taste, aroma and familiar moments that stay with us.

Every course brought something to discover. There was a sense of wonder throughout the evening — at times almost mystical — as familiar flavours, ingredients and memories were presented in entirely new ways.

The service deserves special mention. Attentive without being intrusive, warm without being overly formal, and genuinely personalized. Phillix, Kim and Trish, thank you for taking such wonderful care of us. You helped make the evening feel truly special.

Memory is what remains. And Coco Dining certainly left us with one worth keeping.

🇻🇳 Never thought one meal could make me want to fly back to Ho Chi Minh. Until I found Coco.
Aug 2026 • Friends
I had heard so much about Chef Vương and CoCo Dining, both for the food and the chef’s reputation, so I was very excited to finally experience it myself. After the meal, I completely understood why this restaurant is so highly praised.

CoCo is currently presenting Season 7, LƯU TÍCH: The Living Archive, which explores Vietnamese culinary traditions through five chapters: Cultivation, Preservation, Synthesis, Heirloom and Memory. I really enjoyed how the concept was woven into the food without making the experience feel overly complicated.

Chef Vương’s background also makes the cuisine particularly interesting. Coming from a coastal fishing community, seafood naturally plays an important role in his cooking, while traditional Vietnamese preservation techniques and flavours are reinterpreted through a modern fine dining approach.

My favourite dish was the Fresh Squid with Fermented Squid Sauce, which was also the biggest surprise for me because I normally don’t like squid at all. The squid was stuffed with pork and squid, then served with a rich fermented squid sauce. The flavours were deep and savoury, but everything remained beautifully balanced.

The final Heirloom course, inspired by the Vietnamese family table, was another highlight and a lovely way to end the meal, with rice, dried fish, A5 Wagyu, crab and tomato soup, and mango.

Overall, CoCo completely changed my perception of fine dining in Ho Chi Minh City. The food was thoughtful, creative and deeply connected to Vietnamese culinary heritage, while still feeling contemporary and personal.

A memorable experience, and definitely a restaurant I would return to on my next trip to Ho Chi Minh City.

A very disappointing experience
Jul 2026 • Couples
Upon arrival, we were first seated at the whisky bar for two courses, with the rest of the meals served in the dining area. However, for dessert, we were asked to move to the whisky bar. Perhaps they were in a rush to close. Furthermore, the whisky bar was unsanitary; many small mosquitoes were flying around, and one even stuck to our dessert. The main issue was that we hadn't even eaten it when a staff member came and took it away. A while later, they said the chef had already left and they couldn't make us a new dessert. Their solution was to give us two drinks, but we refused as we had already drunk many and were too full. Their second solution was to give us two coins, saying they would bring us some food next time we returned, but we were leaving Vietnam the next day. I felt their solutions were very insincere, and the service was not what one would expect for the price. So, think carefully before you go!

A real disappointment!
May 2026 • Couples
Last October we went with four of our family to Coco Restaurant, and it was a real delight. 
So we went back yesterday to celebrate a birthday. 
When we booked a table 10 days ago, the only slot available was at 21h. We were happy to book it. We thought they work now in two shifts. 

When we arrived perfectly on time, we saw a more than half empty restaurant! Directly we were thinking, why they did not message us before to tell that they were earlier slots available? They can message for the deposit, for the reconfirmation, but not for something so important. 

Next was the second surprise. We brought a bottle of wine for which we paid last October 1.000.000++ VND. They said yesterday : so sorry, now it’s 2.000.000++ VND! That’s an amount of money you pay in a two/three Michelin star restaurant in Belgium! 

But the worst surprise was the last. 
When we were sitting at the table, they came directly to give the “ a la carte “ menu. 
Asking why the tasting menu was not available anymore, they said last order 20:30h. Even as our reservation was accepted at 21h. 
However, that was not noted in the reservation (see picture below). 
And, they said, please order your main dish in 15 minutes, kitchen is closed!!!

Finally, we got a few bites, they came after three bites to clear the bread and butter already, they were able to bring one wrong main dish, and we just could finish with the bill. 

When asked that the service charge should be dropped because of all what happened, they said, cannot… 

A thoroughly deep disappointment, not worth a Michelin star.
